newsitem.title: UK: Brazil debt said to rise before stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Brazil debt said to rise before stabilising.

text.p: Brazil's national debt as a percentage of GDP is likely to increase by a few percentage points over the next two years before stabilising, a senior central bank official said on Tuesday. "The national debt could increase by a couple of percentage points or more over the next two years," Gustavo Franco, director of international affairs at Brazil's central bank, told a conference of investors in London.

"It is now about one-third of gross domestic product," he added. "It increased last year because of the fiscal deficit and it could increase a bit more over the next two years while we achieve stabilisation of debt to GDP."
On Monday, Brazil's central bank released data putting net public sector debt at 252.701 billion reais, or 35 percent of GDP, but added the trend was towards stabilisation.

A central bank official in Brasilia said the the sharp increase in the debt to GDP ratio since December had been due to the government's policy of high interest rates, currently among the highest in Latin America. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
